docs.title: Cup of Carbon
docs.text:
Cup of Carbon estimates the dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration of water samples from photographs taken with a smartphone. DOC is reported in milligrams per litre (mg/L); darker water often has a higher DOC concentration.

This site contains:

  • A user guide for preparing and photographing samples.
  • A developer guide for previewing and building this documentation.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Site Registration: Users can register at Cup of Carbon to upload samples, create sites and view and delete their own uploads.

  • Sample upload: This feature allows users to upload a top down image of peat water which will be sat on a printed out form, which is available for download. The form contains Aruco codes which allow the system to detect the paper and locate the cup containing the peat water within the paper

  • Sample records: All valid samples are stored within the system and are viewable. Each record contains the DOC value and other meta data as well as a map of the location it was acquired and the image of the upload.

  • Interactive maps: Upon loading of the home page users will be presented with an interactive map that will display all of the samples uploaded to Cup of Carbon. The samples are clickable and records can be accessed via this map.

  • Sites: Registered users are able to add specific sites via an interactive map where they can create a polygon. This allows an samples uploaded to the application to be searched by their site if created.

  • Sample search: Cup of Carbon has a search function which will return records based on search parameters 'Site', 'Date from' and 'Date to'. Search results are returned in the form of interactive map and as a paginated table.

  • Sample download: The results of sample searches can be downloaded as a CSV. If the user wishes for a batch download they can leave all search parameters empty. Registered users can also download a copy of their own samples from their account page.

The method was developed and calibrated using 117 water samples photographed with eight smartphone models. In testing, 95% of measurements were within ±12.3 mg/L of laboratory DOC values (Muir et al., 2025).

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: The application is a Flask web app. Its Python package contains the routes, services, and templates. MongoDB stores application data.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The application follows a server-rendered architecture using Flask and Jinja2.

  1. Flask handles routing, authentication, business logic, and database access.
  2. Jinja2 templates render dynamic HTML pages on the server.
  3. JavaScript provides client-side interactivity where required.
  4. MongoDB stores application data.
Browser
  |
  v
Flask Routes
  |
  +--> Business Logic
  |
  +--> MongoDB
  |
  +--> Jinja2 Templates
          |
          v
      HTML Response

docs.title: Run the application locally
docs.text:
The app connects to mongodb://localhost:27017/colorimetry_db by default. To use a different MongoDB URI, set the MONGO_URI environment variable (in .env) before starting the app.

From the project root, create and activate a virtual environment, then install the application requirements:

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate#     #Linux/macOS
.venv\Scripts\activate         # Windows
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

Create a .env file in the project root (next to run.py). Copy the template and fill in your own values:

| Variable | How to get it |
|---|---|
| `SECRET_KEY` | Generate one: `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"` |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | Register a site at [google.com/recaptcha/admin](https://www.google.com/recaptcha/admin) (add `localhost` as a domain for local use) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Create a key in the [Resend](https://resend.com) dashboard under API Keys |

Never commit .env. It is listed in .gitignore.

Start the Flask development server with:

python run.py

The app will be available at http://127.0.0.1:5000.

docs.title: Preview the documentation
docs.text:
Activate the project virtual environment where MkDocs is installed:

.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
mkdocs serve

MkDocs serves a live preview locally and rebuilds it when documentation files change.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
mkdocs build

MkDocs writes the generated site to site/. Do not edit generated files directly; make changes in docs/ or mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
• A printed, laminated Cup of Carbon background sheet, or one in a clear plastic sleeve.
  • A straight-sided white mug, approximately 300 mL, with an internal depth of 7–9 cm.
  • A flat surface, such as a clipboard.
  • A smartphone or digital camera.
  • A Cup of Carbon account.

docs.title: Create an account
docs.text:
1. Open the Cup of Carbon web app and choose Sign In, then Sign Up Now.
  2. Enter a username (2–6 characters), email address, and password. The password must be at least eight characters and contain an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character. Enter it again to confirm.
  3. Complete the reCAPTCHA and select Sign Up.
  4. After the account is created, sign in with your email address and password.

The registration page says that your email address is used by the Cup of Carbon development team for important app announcements or password-reset assistance, and is not shared beyond the University of Glasgow.

docs.title: Photograph a sample
docs.text:
1. Fill the white mug with the water sample.
  2. Place the mug on the background sheet, aligning its handle with the guide marks.
  3. Keep the setup in even shade. Avoid direct sunlight, glare, and reflections.
  4. Photograph from approximately 30–40 cm above the mug. Include the entire background sheet in the image.
  5. Sign in to the Cup of Carbon web app, choose Upload, submit the photograph, and provide the sampling location or notes if prompted.

docs.title: Improve your results
docs.text:
• Take three to five replicate photographs and average the results.
  • The method performs best for samples in the 0–35 mg/L DOC range.
  • Dilute very dark samples with colourless water before analysis.
  • Filter samples with substantial suspended sediment or peat: this method estimates dissolved, not particulate, organic carbon.
